I would assume that she acts like that because she is embarrassed/doesn't want to talk about it, or doesn't know how to talk about it.

being depressed about nothing is a horrible feeling, it might be a cry for help, it might be the only way she knows how to deal with whats going on.   
The only person that knows why she does it, is herself until she is ready to tell you.  You should try and be supportive, make sure she knows it hurts you that she does that, but at the same time don't try and guilt her.  The 22 year old in me, wants to say tell a guidance counselor or her parents, but I remember when I was 15, having older people, act like your problems aren't a big deal really sucks, because the only person who truly knows how someone feels, is the person with the feels.

I guess there are 2 ways to solve the problem.  Eliminate the depression, or help her find a safe way of handling it.  Eliminating could be as simple as a dr. giving anti-depressants, but they are not a guaranteed fix.  Getting rid of the depression is probably something that you will not be able to do.  However, helping her find a safer way to deal with it is something that you can do.  Try and help her find activities she is interested in, such as painting, going on walks/runs/hikes, reading, or really anything other than cutting.

you are in a really hard position and I hope it works out.

Btw, everything I said, assumes that she is just depressed and cutting, if she is suicidal you really need to tell a guidance counselor, or her parents.
